BEMR_worst_case.context: first observation immediately after the preregistered RISE-to-FALL phase reversal

interpretation: The preregistered C6D support decision remains positive because maximum absolute error and per-interface sign count were descriptive, not adjudication gates.
The exposed transition outlier is retained as mechanism evidence and may not be tuned away.
Any later fresh blind free-running validation must prospectively include fast-transition/tail behavior in addition to pooled error metrics.

scientific_interpretation: Adding the conservation-derived first water-content moment and reconstructing through the mathematically qualified bounded entropy-dual profile materially improves the preregistered primary moving-phase interface-flux vector relative to CURRENT_LAYER_FACE on the same immutable Reference states.
The improvement is not a scalar-tuned effect: both S and M are projected directly from fine Reference water content and BEMR uses the frozen C6C algebraic map with no candidate feedback.
The result supports the hypothesis that the post-C5R propagation limit contains missing subgrid-shape information, not merely insufficient bottom-layer placement.
The result is exposed mechanism evidence, not blind hydrological validation and not evidence of free-running stability.
A pronounced phase-reversal outlier demonstrates that BEMR is not uniformly superior and creates a mandatory future fast-transition/tail-risk validation obligation.

next_authority.question: Can the already-qualified BEMR S/M reconstruction remain realizable, single-branch and hydraulically consistent when the lower external condition is prescribed flux instead of prescribed head, without changing the state, dual order or constitutive interval?
constraints: No hydrological trajectories or C6D response residuals in C6E.
Retain D12_B2P5 all-layer S/M state and the frozen C6C BEMR logistic P3 dual representation.
Use a response-independent synthetic prescribed-flux boundary domain derived prospectively from the existing C6C state domain and B14 constitutive law.
No clipping, regularization, moment localization, dual-order change, constitutive-bound change or response-based tuning.
If prescribed-flux boundary qualification fails, stop before free-running implementation.
If it passes, only then preregister a fresh blind free-running BEMR test with an explicit transition-tail guard informed by the exposed C6D mechanism risk.
